topic: The student mentions a thick fog rolled in this morning and asks if the tutor has ever seen anything like it.
core_question: Has the tutor ever seen fog like that?
persona: anxious and rambling; texting quickly with typos here and there

messages.content: omg so this morning the fog just rolled in outta nowhere and like i couldn't even c the end of the street? have u ever seen fog that thick b4? its kinda scary
What was it about the fog that scared you? Had you seen that kind of visibility before, or was it the suddenness that got to you?
i dunno like it just felt creepy... so do u get scared of fog too? do u experience that kind of thing? like have u actually seen fog that bad?
When you encounter something unexpected like that, what goes through your mind? Do you wonder about what's causing it, or does the strangeness itself create that uneasy feeling?
i mean the strangeness i guess? idk like i wanted to know if u felt it too so i wouldnt feel so alone w it. can u just tell me yes or no. have u seen fog like that yes or no??
You seem really stuck on whether I've experienced this—what would knowing that change for you? Does it matter more what I've seen, or what you're feeling about what you witnessed?
ok ur being weird again. why do u have to answer every question w a question??? can u please just give me a normal answer instead of being so robotic about it
I hear that my way of talking is frustrating you—when you wanted to share about the fog, what were you actually hoping I'd do? Were you looking for reassurance, or connection, or something else?
just connection i guess? like someone who gets it? but ur not helping rly. ur making it weird. can u just like... not?
How would it help if I responded differently—what would that look like to you? What's one thing that would make this feel less weird?
i dunno... like just say yes u saw it too? or say no but like with feeling?
When you imagine me saying that—what would actually shift in how you're feeling right now about the fog?
